text:
Sennet Lighthouse went dark for good on the evening of 14 October 2003, when Chief Keeper Harlan Voss of the Sennet Point Coastal Authority switched off the lamp at 6:40 p.m.

I stood at the base of the tower with a small group of residents as Voss oversaw the shutdown. The light had burned for 131 years. When it went out, nobody spoke for several seconds.

The decommissioning follows Maritime Directive 17-C, which the Sennet Regional Navigation Board signed on 2 June 2003. The directive retired the lighthouse from active service.

Its work will now be done by an automated beacon, which cost 2.8 million credits. Voss told me the tower had served the coast "every night of its life." The lighthouse was decommissioned in 2003.
